DELIBERATE, and the duplication IS the deliverable. ADR-1612's deciding measurement is how many CReal.integral theorems the generic integration space RE-DERIVES rather than assumes, and the only way to make that checkable rather than rhetorical is to declare the same proposition a second time with a proof that is IntSpace.integral_witness_independent applied to IntSpace.crealInterval and nothing else. The two proof terms are genuinely independent: CReal's own route is a converges_unique argument over Riemann sums (creal/integral.rs), the IntSpace route is monotonicity plus CReal.equiv_of_le_le with no Riemann sum anywhere. Aliasing one to the other would destroy the measurement. intspace_tests::the_rederived_statement_equals_creals_own asserts the two rendered types are EQUAL, so this group is not merely tolerated -- it is required to exist and required to stay identical.

Intentional cross-check, and the point of ADR-1607: the SAME statement proved two ways, once through CReal.supOn (metric/compactness.rs, via CReal.evt_approx_max plus And-reassociation) and once through the general metric EVT applied to Metric.creal_totallyBoundedOn_interval and Metric.creal_uniformly_continuous_on (metric/interval.rs). The duplication IS the evidence that the interval EVT is an instance of the metric one -- metric_tests::the_interval_evt_is_the_metric_evt_at_one_type asserts the kernel holds one interned ExprId for both types, with Metric.evt_approx_max's own type as the non-vacuity control. Making either a forwarding alias would delete exactly the fact being claimed. Same shape as the Apollonius entry above.
